clonoview_export

Source: R/clonoview.R
clonoview_export.Rd

Build a self-contained copy of the viewer that opens without R or Python.

Usage

clonoview_export(
  file = "ClonoView-offline.zip",
  datasets = NULL,
  zip = TRUE,
  python = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

file

Path for the zip file to write. The folder is built beside it.

datasets

Datasets to include. Defaults to everything prepared.

zip

Whether to zip the folder. FALSE leaves just the folder.

python

Python interpreter to use. Defaults to [clonoview_python()].

verbose

Whether to print progress.

Value

The path written, invisibly.

Details

Writes a folder holding the viewer and the data it draws, and zips it. The person receiving it double-clicks `ClonoView.html`; there is nothing to install, and it does not use the internet. This is the form to send to a collaborator or a reviewer, or to attach as supplementary material.

The export contains the data, not a picture of it. Per-cell coordinates, cell types, subject identifiers and every clone identifier – which for an immune-repertoire run means the receptor sequences – are all in the folder, because the viewer computes from them in the browser. Treat sending one as publishing that data.

See also

[clonoview_bundle()], [clonoview()]
